correctness.rationale: The max of |x+y| and |x−y| is |x|+|y| over the reals, so Jβ is an isometry. Extending its four coordinate functionals by Hahn–Banach gives a contraction into the canonical cube space for any isometric superspace, so the best canonical retraction realizes the absolute constant. The two sign flips and the swap act by signed permutations of the four input coordinates. Their intertwining relations force the equivariant rows (a,0,b,b) and (0,a,b,−b), with a+2βb=1. The norm is the maximum of the l1 norms of the four support rows after composition, namely |a|+2|b| and 2β(|a|+|b|). The displayed convex combination of these branches is β/q times |a|+2β|b|, so the optimum is at least β/q, and the proposed coefficients attain it. In the interior the convex weights are strictly positive and equality forces both branches equal and a,b nonnegative; their solution is unique. At β=1/2 the first branch is at least 1+|b|; at β=1 the second is at least 1+|a|, giving the unique endpoint coefficient pairs. Averaging all conjugates of any optimal retraction therefore gives the same symmetric optimum. For each displayed norming pair, every conjugate evaluation is bounded by the optimum and their average attains the bound, so the original map also saturates the pair. At each of four input sign vectors the two target supports are independent, with determinant magnitude β, and the four sign vectors span R⁴ with determinant magnitude 8. Hence the total eight-equation determinant has magnitude 64β⁴; this pins down the unrestricted map also at both endpoints. Differentiation gives the stated maximum and endpoint behavior.
residual_risks: Real scalars and uniqueness in the specified four-coordinate superspace only. No claim of uniqueness in every isometric embedding or over complex scalars follows.

evidence: For these symmetric planes, writing r=1/β−1 gives four axis-parallel sides of norm length 2r and four diagonal sides of norm length 2β(1−r), so the self-length is 8(2β²−2β+1)/β, also at the degeneracies by the zero-length sides. The known self-length identity p(X)=8/λ(X) yields the entire numerical profile.
Theorem 5.6 strengthens already unique minimal projections in a complex polytope setting. The frozen proof instead proves uniqueness from independent norming equalities for the optimizer face.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: The perimeter argument determines the optimum objective but not the set of minimizing operators. equivalent_formulations.reasoning: Canonical projection P and retraction R are equivalent by P=JβR. In that formulation the five-coordinate plane is a different range and source dimension, and equivariant uniqueness is insufficient: averaging several different optimum maps could give a single symmetric optimum. The saturation argument imposes conditions on every optimum separately.

The full rank certificate explains that rigidity in the canonical embedding.
